learningObjectives: Apply the naming convention Tosca uses for Request vs. Response Modules and TestCases.
Populate a TestStepValue from a Value Range created earlier in the Module.
Use the Auto fill Values button to populate default values across many TestSteps at once.
Copy values from an external XML/JSON file directly into TestStepValues via the clipboard.

elements.description: Request Modules and TestCases keep the same name as the original Message in the API Scan. Tosca automatically appends "Response" to the Response Module/TestCase name.

elements.text: Numerical prefixes (01, 02...) applied earlier in the API Scan still matter after import — you can drag and drop Modules/TestCases into your preferred order in Tosca, but keeping the prefix makes it easy to identify matching Request/Response pairs at a glance.
The running example for this lesson: add a new coffee shop to the SUT, verify it exists, then delete it — a single TestCase spanning Create, Verify, and Delete.
Official Best Practice: it's best practice to determine a structure and naming convention at the beginning of the project to avoid misunderstandings during testing.

bulletPoints: As with UI TestCases, agree on a naming/structure convention with your whole team up front — and lock it in before the first Module or TestCase is built, not partway through.

elements.description: When multiple values exist for the same Business Parameter (e.g. multiple cities across multiple shops in a Response), highlighting them in the Payload and clicking Add populates the ValueRange column on the corresponding TestCase. This lets you pick any one of those real values from a drop-down in the Value column.

Clicking Auto fill Values on the ribbon, then "from Default", populates the Value field with the Module's default value. It works when either only TestSteps, or only TestStepValues, are selected — not when a TestCase or a mix of TestSteps/TestStepValues is selected.

elements.text: For TestCases with many TestSteps, hold Ctrl to select several TestSteps at once, then click Auto fill Values once to populate them all together.

elements.description: If an XML or JSON file already contains the parameters and values you need in a readable format, select the TestStepValues in Tosca, click "Values", then "from Clipboard" to populate them directly from whatever was copied to the clipboard.

bulletPoints: Value Range = pick from real, previously-seen server values via a drop-down.
Auto fill Values "from Default" only works on a pure TestStep selection or a pure TestStepValue selection — never a mix.
"from Clipboard" is a fast path when your real test data already lives in an external XML/JSON file.

items: It's best practice to determine a structure and naming convention at the beginning of the project to avoid misunderstandings during testing.

examPitfalls.title: Manually renaming every Response Module/TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates think they must manually type "Response" onto every Response Module and TestCase name after import.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Tosca automatically appends "Response" to Response Module/TestCase names on import; Request names simply keep the original Message name from the API Scan.

examPitfalls.title: Selecting a mix of TestSteps and TestStepValues before Auto fill Values
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates select a TestCase, or a mix of TestSteps and TestStepValues, then wonder why the Auto fill Values button is greyed out.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Auto fill Values only works when selecting EITHER only TestSteps OR only TestStepValues — not the TestCase itself, and not a mixed selection.

examPitfalls.title: Manually retyping values that already exist in an external file
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates retype parameter values by hand even though the exact data already exists in a readable XML/JSON file.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Copy the relevant text from the XML/JSON file, select the TestStepValues in Tosca, then use Values > "from Clipboard" to populate them directly.

examPitfalls.title: Deciding on structure/naming convention mid-project
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Candidates assume naming and folder structure can be worked out later, once more Modules and TestCases already exist.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Official course Best Practice: determine a structure and naming convention at the BEGINNING of the project, before building starts, to avoid misunderstandings during testing.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After importing an API Scan Message that was a Response, what does Tosca automatically do to the resulting Module and TestCase names?

options.text: Nothing — the tester must rename them manually.
Appends "Response" to the Message's original name.
Prepends "RSP_" to the Message's original name.

practiceQuiz.hint: Request keeps the original name; Response gets one extra word.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tosca automatically appends the suffix "Response" to the Message name for the Response Module and TestCase. Request Modules/TestCases keep the exact same name as the Message in the API Scan.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester has selected a TestCase and wants to click Auto fill Values to populate default values across all its TestSteps at once. What happens?

options.text: It works — Auto fill Values supports selecting the whole TestCase.
The button is unavailable — Auto fill Values only works with a pure TestStep selection or a pure TestStepValue selection.
It populates only the first TestStep.
It deletes all existing values first, then repopulates them.

practiceQuiz.hint: Selecting the TestCase itself is one of the unsupported selection types.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Auto fill Values button only works when either only TestSteps or only TestStepValues are selected. It's not available if the TestCase itself is selected, or if the selection mixes TestSteps and TestStepValues.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester has real test data sitting in an external JSON file. What is the fastest way to get those exact values into the corresponding TestStepValues in Tosca?

options.text: Manually retype each value by reading from the JSON file.
Select the TestStepValues in Tosca, then use Values > "from Clipboard" after copying the relevant content.
Import the JSON file as a new Component Folder and delete the old TestCase.
This is not possible — external file data cannot be copied into TestStepValues.

practiceQuiz.hint: Copy first, then use a specific button in Tosca's Values menu.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TestStepValues can be populated directly from an XML/JSON file's content by copying the relevant text, selecting the TestStepValues in Tosca, and choosing Values > "from Clipboard".

practiceQuiz.scenario: Per the course's official Best Practice, when should a project's structure and naming convention be decided?

options.text: At the beginning of the project, to avoid misunderstandings during testing.
Only after the Final Exam, since it doesn't affect testing.
Whenever a naming conflict actually occurs.
Tosca enforces one fixed naming convention automatically, so no team decision is needed.

practiceQuiz.hint: This is stated verbatim as a course Key Point.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The course's official Key Point states it's best practice to determine a structure and naming convention at the beginning of the project, to avoid misunderstandings during testing — not partway through, and not only when problems arise.

Highlight multiple real values in the Payload + Add → populates a drop-down of real choices in the TestCase.
Works on a pure TestStep or pure TestStepValue selection — never the TestCase itself or a mixed selection.
Copy real data from an XML/JSON file, select TestStepValues, then Values > from Clipboard.
